key_insight: The current-driven complete electrode model for electrical impedance tomography can be implemented using standard Robin boundary solves coupled through a small electrode system.
engineering_relevance: This formulation enables accurate electrode-voltage calculations in standard FEM packages without requiring a dedicated augmented CEM implementation.
method: Solve prescribed electrode-potential Robin problems to construct an electrode transadmittance matrix.
Enforce total electrode currents through the small electrode system.
Prove equivalence to the augmented CEM and formalise discrete energy, equivalence and reference arguments in Lean 4.
evidence_signal: Across five FEM packages in 2D P1 tests, maximum absolute electrode-potential differences were below 5×10⁻¹³ versus EIDORS and errors below 1.1×10⁻¹³ versus an exact rational-arithmetic reference.
watch_item: Equivalence requires an invertible Robin matrix and identical assembled blocks; implementation also needs consistent electrode-current integration and potential referencing.
paper_title: Implementing the EIT complete electrode model through Robin boundary conditions
